brief: A system monitor where CPU/memory are organisms — healthy breathes steady, stressed pulses fast

dominant_strengths: Clean numeric typography with confident hierarchy; percentage-to-label ratio reads instantly against the deep navy field
Amber/teal duality semantically cues stress vs calm without relying on text, and the soft inner glow hints at a living core
dominant_weaknesses: Two isolated rings on a vast empty canvas — composition feels like a dashboard widget, not a coupled organism ecosystem
Static screenshot cannot prove the breathing/pulsing metaphor; concentric guide rings are decorative rather than rhythm-encoding
Pill labels 'Elevated Activity' / 'Stable Rhythm' are generic captions; nothing visually differentiates an organism from a standard radial gauge
fix_priorities: Encode the metaphor visually: irregular membrane deformation, heartbeat-like radius modulation, or a visible pulse trail per tick
Tighten composition — couple the two organisms (shared field, proximity, reactive coupling) so they feel like one system
Replace concentric guide rings with rhythm-bearing structures (waveform halo, inhale/exhale arcs) that read state at a glance
Add micro-texture or cellular noise inside the orb so it feels biological rather than a CSS conic gradient
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral lands moderately via glow and color, but behavioral feedback is weak in still form and reflective payoff is shallow because the organism metaphor stays nominal.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially solves the brief — color and copy gesture at the organism concept, but without motion or morphology the gauges still read as conventional radial meters.
